policy_title: Reverse Conservative Army Cuts and Increase Defence Spending
stated: Reversing the Conservative Government’s cut to the Army, with a longerterm ambition of increasing regular troop numbers back to over 100,000. Maintaining the UK’s support for NATO, and accordingly increasing defence spending in every year of the Parliament, with an ambition to spend at least 2.5% of GDP on defence.

bearing_set.reason: Reversing army cuts and increasing defence spending directly affects national security posture, defence capability, and resilience to external threats.

Committing to spend at least 2.5% of GDP on defence (up from ~2.3% currently) represents a material increase in public expenditure; if unfunded through offsetting cuts or revenue rises, it directly worsens the debt path / funded-vs-borrowed balance — a concrete O12 indicator.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O5 (the direct security benefit the policy is designed for) and O12 (the fiscal tradeoff — a large, multi-year spending commitment whose funding source is unspecified in the stated policy). Other plausible spillovers (e.g. O13 via defence-industry R&D or O4 via military employment) are too indirect and contested to clear the non-negligible bar without further specifics.
